title: Integration mechanisms
task_statement: Choose an integration mechanism by reuse, trust boundary, and run cost. MCP is not the default for every case. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: MCP connector in the Messages API
components.first_principle: Connect a remote MCP server from the Messages API, so the API calls its tools without a client in your code.
steps: Define each remote server in the mcp_servers array with its URL.
Reference each server from exactly one MCP toolset.
Enable all tools, or allowlist and denylist specific tools in the configs.
Send the request with the MCP connector beta header.
Read the MCP tool use and MCP tool result blocks in the response.
pros: The connector calls remote MCP servers from the Messages API without an MCP client in your code.
One request can connect to several MCP servers.
MCP servers work in Message Batches API requests.
cons: Only the tool calls part of the MCP specification is supported.
A local STDIO server cannot connect directly.
The connector is not covered by zero data retention arrangements.
use_when: A remote server exposes the tools that the app needs.
One host needs a few remote tools and no shared client code. (Inference)
Batch processing needs tool calls against remote servers.
do_not_use_when: The server runs only as a local STDIO process.
Your data policy requires zero data retention for tool data.
The integration needs MCP resources or prompts, because only tools are supported.

constraints.choice: Use an allowlist to expose only approved tools.
constraints.combination: Use a denylist when a server has a few risky tools and many safe ones.

constraints.choice: MCP tool calls in Batches API requests cost the same as in Messages API requests.
constraints.combination: Batch processing gives a 50 percent discount on all usage.

constraints.choice: Connect multiple servers in one request, with one MCP toolset for each server.
constraints.combination: Use tool search when the combined tool count is large.

constraints.choice: Pass a separate authorization_token for each authenticated server.
Check the MCP tool result blocks for errors before you show output to a user. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Verify the tool list in a test request before each release. (Inference)

native_services.text: The MCP connector is listed as beta on this platform.

components.exam_tie: D3.7. Expect a scenario that names the number of hosts and the number of tools. The credited answer matches the mechanism to that reuse count. (Inference)
components.trap: The connector looks like full MCP support. Only tool calls work, so resources and prompts need another path.
components.decision_rule: Use the MCP connector when a Messages API request needs tool calls on a remote MCP server.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario needs MCP resources or prompts, the connector alone does not cover it.

components.name: Claude Code MCP servers
components.first_principle: Register each MCP server once in Claude Code, with a transport that matches where the server runs.

nodes.label: Remote server over HTTP or SSE

steps: Add a remote server with the http transport and its URL.
Add a server that exposes only SSE with the http transport, or with the sse transport before v2.1.265.
Add a local server with the stdio transport and the command after a double dash.
Check the /mcp list for the connection state of each server.
Set a per-server timeout in the server entry when a tool call runs long.
pros: Claude Code connects remote servers over HTTP or SSE, and local servers over STDIO.
Tool search is on by default, which keeps large tool sets out of context.
Organization controls can block a connector tool before Claude sees it.
cons: Without tool search, Claude Code does not report failed server connections to Claude.
A local STDIO server runs as a subprocess on the developer machine. (Inference)
A per-server timeout is a hard wall-clock limit for each tool call.
use_when: A developer needs remote tools in an interactive session.
A local tool exists only as a command-line server. (Inference)
The team needs one shared configuration for several projects. (Inference)
do_not_use_when: The integration runs in production without a developer session. (Inference)
The integration must run in a managed API request, where the MCP connector fits better. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Set an organization control to ask or blocked for a connector tool.
constraints.combination: Use allow rules only for tools that need no prompt. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Set a timeout in the .mcp.json entry for a long server.
constraints.combination: Set CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT to 0 only when idle checks cause false stops. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Keep tool search on for large tool sets.
constraints.combination: Use alwaysLoad only for servers whose tools every turn needs.

constraints.choice: Use a remote server when a shared service must answer for many developers. (Inference)

native_services.text: Not in source. The Claude Code MCP page names no native platform service.

components.exam_tie: D3.7. Expect a scenario about a developer tool that calls a team service. The credited answer names the transport and the configuration scope. (Inference)
components.trap: A local STDIO server looks like a fit for an API backend, but the Messages API connector cannot connect to it directly.
components.decision_rule: Use STDIO for a local process, and HTTP or SSE for a shared remote server.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario names a local command-line tool, choose a Claude Code STDIO server.

key_facts.text: The command claude mcp add --transport http adds a remote HTTP server.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: From v2.1.265, Claude Code tries the HTTP transport first and switches to SSE when the server does not accept it.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Without tool search, Claude Code does not report failed server connections to Claude.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: An organization control set to blocked removes the connector tool before Claude sees it.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The idle timeout defaults to five minutes for HTTP and SSE servers, and to 30 minutes for stdio servers.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The per-server timeout field takes milliseconds and overrides MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT for that server.
key_facts.label: Fact
